title: Bivariate Bubble Relationships: cobubble_test() and contagion_reg()
text: functions look pair series contain, might contain, explosive episode. ask different questions. cobubble_test() (Evripidou, Harvey, Leybourne & Sollis 2022) formal hypothesis test whether explosive episodes y x episode, , whether y_t - alpha - beta * x_{t-} stationary lag lead . KPSS-type test whose null hypothesis co-explosivity (stationary residual). Rejecting null therefore means bubbles two series come underlying process. contagion_reg() (Greenaway-McGrevy & Phillips 2016) formal inference. estimates time-varying contagion coefficient delta_2(r) Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression. point r sample, coefficient measures strongly fixed-window AR(1) coefficient “peripheral” series y moves coefficient “core” series. Neither function returns radf_obj class (see vignette("naming--analysis")).

code: xy <- sim_coexplosive(n = 100, seed = 123) res <- cobubble_test(xy$y, xy$x, nboot = 199, seed = 1) res #>  #> ── cobubble_test (lag = 0, nboot = 199) ──────────────────────────────────────── #>  #> S = 0.2364, cv(95%) = 0.4048, p-value = 0.1508 #> Co-explosivity not rejected at the 5% level. cobubble_test(sim_data$psy1, sim_data$psy2, nboot = 199, seed = 1) #>  #> ── cobubble_test (lag = -2, nboot = 199) ─────────────────────────────────────── #>  #> S = 1.533, cv(95%) = 0.2998, p-value = 0 #> Co-explosivity rejected at the 5% level.

what: A different question from “is there a bubble”
title: Root Inference: How Fast Is the Bubble Growing
text: radf(), datestamp() dating_*(), _test(), monitor() monitor_*() families answer version question whether bubble happened. None says anything magnitude. explosive episode dated, fast underlying autoregressive root growing? rootstamp() (Phillips & Magdalinos 2007; Guo, Sun & Wang 2019) answers question. follow-step detection dating, replaces neither. function fits -intercept AR(1), y_t = rho * y_{t-1} + e_t, given sub-sample. reports estimate rho confidence interval implied doubling time, log(2) / log(rho), number periods bubble needs double size estimated growth rate. two methods two starting points. default method takes numeric sub-sample fits , one confidence interval. radf_obj method takes radf_obj together datestamp() result fits every episode , manual loop. Neither method returns radf_obj class, rootstamp() work summary(), tidy() autoplot() (see vignette("naming--analysis")).

what: Detect, date, then estimate the root
title: Root Inference: How Fast Is the Bubble Growing
text: series unit-root run-followed explosive regime rho = 1.04: first detect date episode usual way: estimate root detected episode. default method takes sub-sample directly, slice Start End episode: estimate rho close true value 1.04. output also reports rho_ci implied doubling_time doubling_time_ci. two interval types answer slightly different questions. type = "normal", default, safer choice drift weak dependence, gives noticeably tighter interval . type = "cauchy" assumes fixed root drift. Cauchy distribution much fatter tails normal one, interval visibly wider even nominal level.
code: y <- sim_psy1(n = 100, te = 60, tf = 100, c = 0.04, alpha = 0, sigma = 1, seed = 2026) r <- radf(y, minw = 20) cv <- radf_mc_cv(length(y), minw = 20, nrep = 300, seed = 4) ds <- datestamp(r, cv = cv, min_duration = 3) ds #>  #> ── Datestamp (min_duration = 3) ───────────────────────────────── Monte Carlo ── #>  #> series1 : #>   Start Peak End Duration   Signal Ongoing #> 1    63  100 100       38 positive    TRUE ep <- ds[["series1"]] rootstamp(y[ep$Start[1]:ep$End[1]]) # normal-t interval (Guo, Sun & Wang 2019), true rho = 1.04 #>  #> ── rootstamp (n = 37, sig_lvl = 95%, type = normal) ──────────────────────────── #>  #>    rho         se  t_stat  rho_lower  rho_upper  doubling_time  dt_lower #>   1.04  0.0007295    54.2      1.038      1.041          17.87     17.26 #>   dt_upper #>      18.53 rootstamp(y[ep$Start[1]:ep$End[1]], type = "cauchy") # fixed-root Cauchy interval (Phillips & Magdalinos 2007) #>  #> ── rootstamp (n = 37, sig_lvl = 95%, type = cauchy) ──────────────────────────── #>  #>    rho         se  t_stat  rho_lower  rho_upper  doubling_time  dt_lower #>   1.04  0.0007295    54.2     0.7955      1.284          17.87     2.776 #>   dt_upper #>      -3.03

title: Simulation
text: PSY validate GSADF test price built Lucas-model fundamentals plus Evans (1991) bubble. sim_div() produces fundamental price random walk drift dividends, using default S&P 500 parameterization West (1988). sim_evans() produces bubble term, scaling factor kappa sets much price bubble accounts :  radf() find episodes:

title: Volatility-Robust Alternatives to radf()
text: Plain radf() assumes constant innovation variance. Real series rarely one, volatility varies time standard critical values longer control size test. exuber offers several fixes, takes structurally different approach. Four five covered (radf_sign(), radf_sign_dm(), radf_kp() radf_sbz()) keep radf_obj class support summary(), datestamp(), tidy() autoplot() way plain radf(). vignette("naming--analysis") shows plugs pipeline validated . radf_sbz_union() exception. bundles statistic radf_sbz() classic supDF one union--rejections call class, radf_obj, print() autoplot() apply. time-deformation approach radf_tt() vignette, vignette("radf-tt"), one covers rest. functions target non-stationary volatility, meaning permanent shift trend unconditional innovation variance. target stationary GARCH-type conditional heteroskedasticity, whose variance profile asymptotically flat leaves plain radf() correct size. running example therefore sim_psy1() bubble driven sim_vol_break() innovations, whose standard deviation triples half-way sample. case plain radf() -rejects :

code: # \donttest{ rsim_data <- radf(sim_data_wdate) #> Using `date` as index variable.  autoplot(rsim_data) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # Modify facet_wrap options through ellipsis autoplot(rsim_data, scales = "free_y", dir = "v") #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # Modify the shading options autoplot(rsim_data, shade_opt = shade(fill = "pink", opacity = 0.5)) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # Allow for nonrejected series to be plotted autoplot(rsim_data, nonrejected = TRUE) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # Remove the shading completely (2 ways) autoplot(rsim_data, shade_opt = NULL) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.  autoplot(rsim_data, shade_opt = shade(opacity = 0)) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # Plot only the series with the shading options autoplot2(rsim_data) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.  autoplot2(rsim_data, trunc = FALSE) # keep the minw period #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # We will need ggplot2 from here on out library(ggplot2)  # Change (overwrite) color, size or linetype autoplot(rsim_data) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "black")) +   scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(0.9, 1)) +   scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "solid")) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`. #> Scale for colour is already present. #> Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale. #> Scale for linewidth is already present. #> Adding another scale for linewidth, which will replace the existing scale. #> Scale for linetype is already present. #> Adding another scale for linetype, which will replace the existing scale.   # Change names through labeller (first way) custom_labels <- c("psy1" = "new_name_for_psy1", "psy2" = "new_name_for_psy2") autoplot(rsim_data, labeller = labeller(.default = label_value, id = as_labeller(custom_labels))) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # Change names through labeller (second way) custom_labels2 <- series_names(rsim_data) names(custom_labels2) <- custom_labels2 custom_labels2[c(3, 5)] <- c("Evans", "Blanchard") autoplot(rsim_data, labeller = labeller(id = custom_labels2)) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # Or change names before plotting series_names(rsim_data) <- LETTERS[1:5] autoplot(rsim_data) #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.   # Change Theme options autoplot(rsim_data) +   theme(legend.position = "right") #> Using precomputed critical values for `cv`.  # }

title: Simulation of a Blanchard (1979) / Rotermann-Wilfling (2018) bubble process — sim_blan
text: Blanchard's bubble process (type = "blanchard") two regimes, occur probability \(\pi\) \(1-\pi\). first regime, bubble grows exponentially, whereas second regime, bubble collapses white noise. probability \(\pi\): $$B_{t+1} = \frac{1+r}{\pi}B_t+\epsilon_{t+1}$$ probability \(1 - \pi\): $$B_{t+1} = \epsilon_{t+1}$$ r positive constant \(\epsilon \sim iid(0, \sigma^2)\). bubble Rotermann & Wilfling (2018) (type = "rotermann_wilfling") replaces "collapse white noise" regime partial, stochastically evolving deflation. trajectories recur periodically deflate gradually instead collapsing abruptly one period: $$B_t = \frac{B_{t-1}u_t}{\delta}$$ probability \(\pi\), $$B_t = \frac{1-\pi\delta}{1-\pi}B_{t-1}u_t$$ probability \(1-\pi\), \(u_t \sim iid\,LN(-rw\_sigma^2/2,\ rw\_sigma^2)\) (\(E[u_t] = 1\)). \(\delta \(0, 1)\) ensures bubble never collapses exactly zero can inflate .

"new stochastic bubble process: Theoretical properties empirical tests." Applied Economics Letters, 25(15), 1091-1096. used Monte Carlo power analysis Monschang, V. & Wilfling, B. (2021). "Sup-ADF-style bubble-detection methods test." Empirical Economics, 61, 145-172.

title: Simulation of a single-bubble process — sim_psy1
text: data generating process described following equation: $$X_t = X_{t-1}1\{t < \tau_e\}+ \delta_T X_{t-1}1\{\tau_e \leq t\leq \tau_f\} + \left(\sum_{k=\tau_f+1}^t \epsilon_k + X_{\tau_f}\right) 1\{t > \tau_f\} + \epsilon_t 1\{t \leq \tau_f\} $$ autoregressive coefficient \(\delta_T\) given : $$\delta_T = 1 + cT^{-}$$ \(c>0\), \(\alpha \(0,1)\), \(\epsilon \sim iid(0, \sigma^2)\) \(X_{\tau_f} = X_{\tau_e} + X'\) \(X' = O_p(1)\), \(\tau_e = [T r_e]\) dates origination bubble, \(\tau_f = [T r_f]\) dates collapse bubble. pre- post- bubble periods, \([1, \tau_e)\), \(X_t\) pure random walk process. bubble expansion period \([\tau_e, \tau_f]\) becomes mildly explosive process expansion rate given autoregressive coefficient \(\delta_T\); , finally post-bubble period, \((\tau_f, \tau]\)  \(X_t\) reverts martingale. details see Phillips et al. (2015) p. 1054.

title: Simulation of a single-bubble process — sim_psy1

title: Simulation of a two-bubble process — sim_psy2
text: two-bubble data generating process given (see also sim_psy1): $$\begin{aligned} X_t = {} & X_{t-1}1\{t \N_0\}+ \delta_T X_{t-1}1\{t \B_1 \cup B_2\} + \left(\sum_{k=\tau_{1f}+1}^t \epsilon_k + X_{\tau_{1f}}\right) 1\{t \N_1\} \\ & + \left(\sum_{l=\tau_{2f}+1}^t \epsilon_l + X_{\tau_{2f}}\right) 1\{t \N_2\} + \epsilon_t 1\{t \N_0 \cup B_1 \cup B_2\} \end{aligned}$$ autoregressive coefficient \(\delta_T\) : $$\delta_T = 1 + cT^{-}$$ \(c>0\), \(\alpha \(0,1)\), \(\epsilon \sim iid(0, \sigma^2)\), \(N_0 = [1, \tau_{1e})\), \(B_1 = [\tau_{1e}, \tau_{1f}]\), \(N_1 = (\tau_{1f}, \tau_{2e})\), \(B_2 = [\tau_{2e}, \tau_{2f}]\), \(N_2 = (\tau_{2f}, \tau]\), \(\tau\) last observation sample. observations \(\tau_{1e} = [T r_{1e}]\) \(\tau_{1f} = [T r_{1f}]\) origination termination dates first bubble; \(\tau_{2e} = [T r_{2e}]\) \(\tau_{2f} = [T r_{2f}]\) origination termination dates second bubble. collapse first bubble, \(X_t\) resumes martingale path time \(\tau_{2e}-1\), second episode exuberance begins \(\tau_{2e}\). Exuberance lasts \(\tau_{2f}\), point process collapses value \(X_{\tau_{2f}}\). process continues martingale path end sample period \(\tau\). duration first bubble assumed longer second bubble, .e. \(\tau_{1f}-\tau_{1e}>\tau_{2f}-\tau_{2e}\). details can refer Phillips et al., (2015) p. 1055.

title: Simulation of a stochastic branching-tree bubble — sim_tree
text: stochastic intensity \(p_t = \Phi(X_t)\), \(X_t\) latent stationary Gaussian AR(1): $$X_t = \mu + \rho(X_{t-1}-\mu) + \sigma\sqrt{1-\rho^2}u_t,\quad u_t \sim iid\,N(0,1)$$ Given \(p_t\), draw \(Z_t \sim Bernoulli(p_t)\) set (paper's eq. 5-6): $$Y_t = \xi_{1t}Y_{t-1}+\epsilon_t,\quad \xi_{1t}=\frac{1}{}\frac{Z_t}{p_t},\quad \epsilon_t=\frac{\eta}{1-}\left(1-\xi_{1t}\right)+\frac{\eta}{}\frac{1-Z_t}{1-p_t}$$ \(>1\) controls growth rate active phase branch, \(\eta>0\) sets price floor \(\eta/(1-)\) (Corollary 1 source: \(Y_t \ge \eta/(1-)\)), \(\rho\) controls persistence bubble-growth phase, \(\sigma\) controls frequency bubbles. process finite mean (Proposition 3 source), occasional large values feature model bug. default parameters (\(\mu=-1,\eta=1,=0.95,\sigma=4,\rho=0.7\)) reproduce illustrative example source (Section 2.3, Figure 2).

title: exuber 2.0.0
text: radf_sbz(), radf_sbz_cv() radf_sbz_union() implement WLS/kernel-volatility SBZ test Herwartz & Siedenburg. test split statistic (radf_sbz()), bootstrap critical values (radf_sbz_cv(), full datestamp() autoplot() support) union--rejections test classic supDF (radf_sbz_union()). union test original bundled radf_sbz_cv() renamed. See vignette("volatility-robust-radf"). radf_kp() kernel-purge heteroskedasticity test. radf_wb_cv(..., dist_skew = TRUE) skewness-corrected wild bootstrap Hafner (2020). radf_sign() radf_sign_cv() implement sign-based sGSADF Harvey, Leybourne & Zu (2020), invariant volatility needs bootstrap. ssu_test() implements stochastic explosive-coefficient tests Kurozumi & Nishi (2025): SSU, GSSU (type = "gssu", double recursion window starts). union = TRUE adds union rejections paper (UR/GUR) SADF/GSADF. critical values come Table paper. cusum_test() implements retrospective CUSUM tests Kurozumi & Nishi (2025) ("cs", "gcs") two-sided CUSUM--squares tests ("cssq", "gcssq"). datestamp(..., option = "svadf") implements SV-ADF asymmetric-threshold dating Sarkar & Wells (2026). added option datestamp() separate radf_svadf() function. source preprint peer reviewed. caveat shown function called Caveats section ?datestamp.

title: exuber 2.0.0
text: dating_pdc() implements PDC/KS sequential sample-splitting dating. type = "wls" adds correction Kurozumi & Skrobotov (2023) time-varying volatility. radf_recovery() radf_recovery_cv() implement reverse-regression dating crisis origination recovery Phillips & Shi (2014). f_c overall false-detection rate exploratory validated . flagged function called ?radf_recovery. dating_hls() implements SSR/BIC single-bubble dating Harvey, Leybourne & Sollis (2017). dating_hlw() implements two-step SSR/BIC multi-bubble wrapper Harvey, Leybourne & Whitehouse (2020), including run-joining rule paper fragmented step-1 detections (join = 3; 0 disables ). dating_knp() implements bias-corrected dating Kejriwal, Nguyen & Perron (2025). breaks argument dates several bubbles dynamic programme paper, finds exact global minimizer O(breaks * n^2).

title: exuber 2.0.0
text: monitor() implements training monitoring procedure Phillips & Shi (2020) (Family ). adds closed-form SADF GSADF_s0 boundaries Kurozumi (2020) FLUC boundary Homm & Breitung (2012). monitor_cusum() implements CUSUM monitoring Homm & Breitung (2012). adds volatility-robust CUSUMV kernel variant Astill et al. (2023) finite-sample boundary Homm & Breitung. lbi_test() monitor_lbi() implement static LBI test Breitung & Diegel (2025) sequential mCUSUM/wCUSUM extension.

title: exuber 2.0.0
text: radf_common() radf_common_cv() implement common-bubble detection Chen, Phillips & Shi (PCA followed PSY). cobubble_test() implements co-explosivity test Evripidou, Harvey, Leybourne & Sollis (2022). contagion_reg() implements bubble contagion regression Greenaway-McGrevy & Phillips (2016), minimal subset paper.

title: exuber 2.0.0

Away median oversized small samples, QPSY badly oversized. caveat message call time says .

title: exuber 2.0.0

Parallel runs (options(exuber.parallel = TRUE)) now reuse one worker cluster per session. , every call started stopped fresh future::multisession, start-time seconds dominated every small radf_mc_cv() radf_wb_cv() job. exuber.ncores sets size cluster, cluster stopped namespace unloads. exuber.parallel now defaults interactive(). Scripts, knitr R CMD check therefore run serially unless opt , batch job longer pays worker start-leaves worker connections open handful replications. panel statistic radf() used apply(bsadf, 1, mean). dispatch overhead call grows number rows. 65 times slower equivalent rowMeans(bsadf) n = 100 289 times slower n = 1000, largest single part runtime radf() every sample size tested. replaced rowMeans(bsadf), gives identical result. tests/testthat unchanged, 879 tests passing.
